brief: Goldman's Molavi frames markets as volatile and directionless, with AI-driven news flow causing violent risk-on/risk-off rotation that makes running gross and net exposure difficult; the desk anchors on AI, oil and yields, leaning on megacap strength and narrowness. France's budget standoff has pushed the OAT-bund spread to 140bps, the widest since 1990, raising European contagion concern. Equity issuance is showing fatigue (deals pulled) even as Broadcom and SpaceX raise capital for AI capex, and hyperscaler debt has topped $500bn this year, with Oracle, SpaceX and Nvidia CDS pricing meaningful default risk. Middle East escalation (Riyadh airport attacks) pushed oil higher before G7 reserve releases and a Trump/Putin diesel deal; those relief tools are running dry, so Molavi sees oil struggling to normalize lower and skewed higher via refining, logistics and insurance costs. Separately, GPU pricing is rising 17-21% on scarcity, the top 5 S&P names are 30% of the index, and historically capex peaks lag equity peaks by months to years after a central bank policy shift, which has now begun.
